summary.intent: Continue and complete GSD Phase 72 (SDK Write-Plane Durability and Correctness) end-to-end — planning, execution, and shipping — while first triaging and fixing unrelated CI regressions (desktop-e2e, web-e2e, sdk-e2e) that surfaced mid-session and blocked progress, then ship the phase via PR review, security audit, and merge.
summary.outcome: Phase 72 was fully planned (10 plans, 6 SCs), executed (all waves green), hardened per user directives (test-file typecheck added to CI, 36 skipped tests reduced to 3, a DoS cycle-guard bug fixed), security/CodeRabbit-reviewed (a HIGH moveItem write-chain resurrection bug and several D-09 zeroization gaps found and fixed), and shipped as PR #602, merged to main at c21f896b6. Two prior CI regressions were also fixed and merged (PR #601 FUSE fix, PR #600 web/sdk-e2e fixes).

repo: GSD todo lifecycle: addressed todos move from .planning/todos/pending/ to completed/ by git-mv (not a separate 'resolved/' folder); phases can ship without retiring their source todos, causing drift
IPNS anti-equivocation gate (Phase 71): rejects same-sequence republish with a different CID (HTTP 400) — FUSE per-file publish must resolve-before-first-publish to avoid tripping it on a re-key

Playwright web-e2e: ciFloor() helper only raises wait timeouts to a 60s floor under CI (process.env.CI) — local runs use the raw (often 15-30s) timeout, causing local-only flakes on IPNS-gated mutations that pass fine in CI
vitest does not load .env — sdk-e2e's SDK_E2E_SECRET must be explicitly exported into the shell env or it falls back to a hardcoded default and gets 401'd against a real API

Cross-package types in this monorepo resolve via workspace-symlinked dist (no tsconfig path aliases/project references), so a build-first-then-typecheck ordering is required — typecheck can't run before dependents are built

tsconfig.build.json excludes test files from the production build's tsc, so pnpm typecheck (which shells to each package's build) never caught test-file type errors — root cause of a long-undetected vitest v2→v3 Mock-generics + Phase-62 retired-type drift across 15 test files
WriteChildRef (write-plane, keyed by node UUID/childId) vs SealedChildRef (read-plane, keyed by ipnsName) must never be conflated — a recurring class of bugs in this phase

Base-aware CAS-merge (registration.ts updateFolderMetadataAndPublish) requires baseWriteChildren to be threaded through by EVERY write-chain-mutating caller (delete, restore, move) or a concurrent writer's stale snapshot can resurrect a dropped WriteChildRef — moveItem was missed in the original phase scope and only caught by post-hoc security review

D-09 terminal-owner zeroization: only the terminal owner of a borrowed key buffer zeroes it, in a finally block covering every exit path including throws; borrowing helpers (walkChildWriteKey, hasRealWriteKey, wrapIpnsKeyForTee) must never zero

dfsFindFolder already had a visited-Set cycle guard that collectDescendantIpnsNames lacked, allowing unbounded recursion (DoS) on a cyclic/malicious folder graph — sibling-function asymmetry is worth auditing when hardening one traversal function
Local API on :3000 running from stale dist/main rejects the current TEST_LOGIN_SECRET/.env values silently (401) — must restart from source (nest start --watch) after any secret/env change

code.finding: moveItem's source-folder publish dropped the moved child's WriteChildRef via filter() but never threaded baseWriteChildren into updateFolderMetadataAndPublish, unlike deleteItem/restoreFromBin — allowing a concurrent CAS-409 retry to resurrect the dropped write-link via the legacy naive-union merge fallback (fixed in 65024c3ce)

Base-aware CAS-merge originally only protected local's own deletes from a stale remote copy (asymmetric); it always kept everything present in local regardless of remote, so a childId concurrently deleted by a remote writer got silently resurrected. Rewritten as a symmetric 3-way prune: base-absent entries always kept (concurrent adds), base-present entries kept only if present on BOTH local and remote (fixed in 3b45a0f60)

collectDescendantIpnsNames lacked the visited:Set<string> cycle guard that its sibling dfsFindFolder already had, allowing unbounded recursion on a cyclic folder graph (DoS-class); fixed by threading a shared visited set marked before any await, across all 3 root call sites (fix 2616e96f0)

restoreFromBin's AEAD unseal/reseal during cross-folder re-homing was wrapped in the same fail-open catch as the legitimate resolve-miss fallback, silently downgrading a tampered/wrong-key write-body failure into a read-only restore instead of throwing; and the source-side stale-ref cleanup publish was unguarded, so a transient failure there could abort an already-durably-committed restore. Both fixed in 109b0b051 (AEAD scoped to fail-closed, cleanup made best-effort)
New shared module (72-10) unifying getWriteBodyParams/adoptPublishedFolderState/hasRealWriteKey previously duplicated between client.ts and bin/index.ts; client.ts's copies became thin delegators

workflow: When a background local test run cascades on an unrelated early-test flake, don't just retry — diagnose why the local timeout is tighter than CI's (ciFloor asymmetry here) and either fix the timeout at source or run under CI=1 with a temporarily-patched webServer.reuseExistingServer to get a representative local signal

Dispatching workflow_dispatch-only CI e2e workflows against a feature branch (gh workflow run <file> --ref <branch>, not -f ref=) lets you get real CI-parity validation before merge when the workflow doesn't trigger on pull_request

After merging a dependency PR, rebase (not just leave) a sibling PR branch onto the new main before dispatching validation runs, so the validation reflects the true merge state (desktop-e2e would have failed on stale FUSE code otherwise)

Delegate independent read-heavy diagnostic/verification work to parallel background agents, but adversarially re-verify their conclusions yourself before trusting them for high-blast-radius changes (the F5 merge rewrite was independently traced across all 8 base/local/remote cases by the orchestrator before accepting the security reviewer's 'sound' verdict was actually wrong)

Security review + CodeRabbit CLI + PR-level CodeRabbit re-review each caught different real bugs (moveItem resurrection, remote-delete resurrection, D-09 zeroization gaps, restoreFromBin fail-open) — running all three sequentially before merge, with live sdk-e2e re-validation after each round of fixes, surfaced issues no single pass would have caught

Capture scope-adjacent findings as durable todos with file refs immediately (before they're lost to context) rather than fixing everything inline — keeps the ship gate from scope-creeping into an open-ended audit
Reword non-conventional executor commit subjects via git filter-branch --msg-filter (rebase -i unavailable in this environment) and verify tree-identical before force-push

friction: Multiple GSD hook-fragment JSON files contained raw unescaped newlines/control characters inside string values, breaking both --raw parsing and a hand-written extraction script; had to write a lenient custom parser

Local web-e2e verification hit a whack-a-mole of different tests flaking at different local timeout ceilings across 5+ re-runs (4.10 → 4.11 → 2.1) before switching to a CI=1 + temp-patched webServer.reuseExistingServer regime that finally gave a representative signal

sdk-e2e 401 errors required two rounds of diagnosis: first a stale API dist (fixed by restart from source), then discovering vitest doesn't load .env (had to export SDK_E2E_SECRET manually) — the API not logging handled 4xx bodies made root-causing slower
gh workflow run -f ref=... returned HTTP 422 because main's workflow definition predated that input; had to switch to --ref <branch>
Git commit helper reported false-negative commit_failed several times despite the commit actually landing, requiring manual git log verification each time
Network i/o timeouts on gh workflow run and gh api pulls/reviews calls required retries
Investigating an unrecognized commit on the shared branch (turned out to be the user's own unrelated cleanup commit) added an extra diagnostic detour mid-ship
